list: The official 55 trophies, as published by PlayStation and listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles on 2026-11-18. Names, descriptions and grades are the official ones; the counts (PSN targets) are the ones PSNProfiles lists. Every guide below is written for this entry, in our own words, from the official description alone unless a source says otherwise.

sources.label: PSNProfiles — trophy list and PSN counts

trophies.guide: Earn the other 54 trophies and this one pops with the last of them. There is no shortcut and no separate task of its own, so treat it as the finish line of the roadmap: clear the one-time story moments first, then work the activities, collectibles and money trophies in free roam, and save the 100% completion push for last. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the order is our own advice from the official descriptions.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first story mission, so it pops early in any normal playthrough — just play the opening through and do not skip its objectives. Treat it as a one-time moment: the opening mission only happens once, and whether it can be earned again on a mission replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the one-time warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapters are story progress, not a free-roam task, so keep playing the story and it comes on its own. It is tied to a single chapter, so if you replay missions, check whether chapter trophies pop on replay — that is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Like the other chapter trophies it follows story progress and cannot be ground out in free roam. Because it is tied to one chapter, do not assume a replayed mission re-awards it — that is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. It is pure story progress, so there is nothing to prepare and nothing to grind — just keep the story moving. As with the other chapter trophies, whether it pops on a replayed mission is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4; the trophy pops when the chapter closes, leaving only the finale. By this point the story trophies are a matter of finishing what you started — no side task feeds into them. Whether chapter trophies pop on a mission replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final mission of the story. It is the gold story trophy and the last story beat, so before you start it, clear every other one-time story moment you still need — after the credits roll, free roam may not take you back to them. Whether the finale can be replayed for a missed trophy is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Named-mission trophies like this one pop when that one mission ends, so play it through and finish its objectives rather than rushing past them. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions tend to have setup steps of their own, so follow the mission as it is given and finish it in one go. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like the other named-mission trophies it pops when that mission ends, so there is no separate grind — play the mission and finish it. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The name suggests a set-piece mission, so expect it to be a story beat you play once rather than a task you can repeat at will. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. The airport also figures in the unscheduled-departure trophy, so pay attention while you are there — a mission location can hold more than one trophy moment. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation name suggests a bigger set-piece, so play it through carefully rather than rushing it. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion in the game's own checklist — story, side missions, activities and collectibles together. This is the long trophy: do not chase it first. Finish the story, clear the one-time moments, then use this tracker to mop up whatever the completion counter still shows missing. What exactly the game's 100% counter counts is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the order is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts; PSN tracks the total to 250, so this is a volume trophy that builds up across the whole game. Fold stunt driving into everything else — jumps, airtime and near misses while travelling between missions — rather than grinding it in one sitting. Exactly which moves the game counts as a stunt is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 250; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity once; PSN tracks 9 activity types, so the trophy pops on the ninth different kind you sample. Work through the activities the list already names — racing, fishing, the shooting range, the arcade, bowling, meditation, drone races — and try any other activity the game offers until the count completes. Which 9 types the counter recognises is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 9; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges; PSN tracks the count to 42. This is the most demanding silver: treat the range as a skill to build up, learn each challenge's scoring, and return to the hard ones after you have golded the easy ones — a bronze or silver medal does not count. The medal thresholds for each challenge are not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 42; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations; PSN tracks the count to 14. Drone races are a per-location win, so work through the map location by location and tick each one off here as you win it — a loss at a location just means racing it again. Where the 14 locations are is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 14; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races; PSN tracks the count to 20, and each race only counts once, so variety matters more than repeats. Race a new event each time rather than re-running one you have already won, and keep a faster car for the events that give you trouble. Which events count as races is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 20; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the game's activities, and Cal is the rival the description names — take the challenge when it is offered and out-fish him. If you lose, a fishing challenge can be tried again, so keep at it. Where and when Cal's challenge is offered is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any arcade game counts, so pick the shortest or easiest one you find and play it through — the trophy is for finishing, not for a high score. Which arcade games the game offers and where they are is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. Contact finales are side-story beats: follow Andy's missions to their end and the trophy pops with the last one. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's strand. Like the other contact finales it pops when that strand's last mission ends, so keep Kenton's missions going alongside the story rather than leaving them all to the end. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's strand. The name reads like a biker strand, so expect Billy's missions to come to you as you explore — answer them when they appear rather than hunting for them all at once. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida; PSN tracks the count to 8. Strangers and Freaks missions appear as you explore the state, so take them when you meet them — a stranger met and ignored may not wait. This is a silver, so expect some strands to run several missions long. Which strangers offer strands is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 8; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's strand. Follow Randy's missions to their end; the trophy pops with the last one, like the other contact finales. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's strand. Follow Tyrone's missions to their end; the trophy pops with the last one, like the other contact finales. It is tied to a single mission, so whether it pops on a replay is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the replay warning is our own reading of the official description.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida; PSN tracks the count to 18. Spots are spread over the state, so treat this as an exploration trophy: meditate at each spot you find and tick it off here. Where the 18 spots are is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 18; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. The description names a specific animal for a specific person, so this is a hunting task with a target — take Bret's job, track the animal and bring it down. What the animal is and where it roams is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets; PSN tracks the count to 3. Cards are a collectible: gather full sets rather than scattering your effort, and finish one set before starting the next so progress stays visible. Where the cards are is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 3; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations; PSN tracks the count to 100, so this is a long sweep of the map. Fold it into exploration: WAiNK It wherever you go and the count climbs on its own — do not leave it as a 100-stop grind for the end. What WAiNK It does at a location is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 100; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges; PSN tracks the count to 50. Challenges are the game's small objectives, so this one accumulates as you play everything else — racing, stunts, activities and side tasks all feed it. Pick off the easy challenges early and let the count build. Which tasks count as challenges is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 50; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Build a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you, then lose the cops and escape. The partner matters: do this while playing together, not solo. Break line of sight, hide until the stars fade, and keep your partner with you until you are clear. How the partner system works in free roam is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner and keep your wanted level through all three — losing it means the run is over and you start again. Plan a route between three close shops, rob fast, and keep moving; do not stop to fight the police between stops. Which shops count is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles; PSN tracks the count to 100. Discovery means finding a vehicle type for the first time, so drive and ride everything you see — common cars, bikes, boats and anything unusual — and the count climbs as you explore. Which vehicles count as discovered is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 100; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during a single use of Combat Focus. Set it up: gather a group of enemies first, then trigger Combat Focus when they are close together and finish five before it ends. A quiet street will not do — pick a fight with enough enemies in it. How Combat Focus is triggered and how long it lasts is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — leave the airport by a route no flight schedule offers. The description reads like a one-time stunt at a specific place, so treat it as a moment to plan, not something to stumble into: get to VCIA with a fast vehicle or aircraft and leave on your own terms. What exactly counts as an unscheduled departure is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Rhinos are tanks, and the description is a joke, not an instruction. Something with a Rhino tank earns this one — driving one, destroying one, or surviving one — but which of those the game counts is not yet checked in the game, so do not guess: try the obvious interaction when a Rhino appears and see what pops. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the admission that the trigger is unknown is our own, from the official description.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and stay undetected from entry to exit. Stealth is the whole trophy: plan the approach, avoid cameras and staff sightlines, and leave before anyone raises the alarm — being spotted voids the attempt. Whether a failed attempt can be retried at the same store is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape from each one; PSN tracks the count to 5. Vault robberies are bigger jobs than shop robberies, so plan the escape before the entry — a fast car and a route out matter as much as the robbery itself. Where the vaults are is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 5; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks roam the roads, so watch for one, hit it, and get clear before the police close in — the escape is half the trophy. Whether armored trucks appear on a schedule or at random is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida; PSN tracks the count to 52. This is the map-completion trophy: visit every named area of the state, and use the in-game map to spot the areas you have not been to yet. It pairs naturally with the meditation spots, WAiNK locations and vehicle discoveries. Which 52 areas the counter lists is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 52; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs; PSN tracks the count to 9. Each gang's operation is a separate job, so work through the gangs one at a time and tick each off here — hitting the same gang twice does not advance the count. Which operations belong to which gang is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 9; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. The place is named in the description — Ocean Beach — so head there, find a spot with a view, and order a cocktail. It is a small moment trophy, the kind you pick up while exploring rather than grinding. Which bar or spot counts is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The description reads like a scripted story moment — a showroom, a car, and a wall that was never meant to stop you — so treat it as one-time and do not rush past it when the moment comes. Which showroom it is is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The place is named in the description, so go to that alley and bowl — follow-through suggests finishing a game there, not just rolling one ball. Where the alley is is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The description gives no objective — a partnership with mass appeal. It reads like a story or partnership moment, so it will most likely pop as the story's partnership develops rather than from anything you can grind in free roam. What triggers it is not yet checked in the game, and this guide will not invent a step for it. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the admission that the trigger is unknown is our own, from the official description.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count to 500, so this is a long accumulation of decisions across the whole game, not one moment. Play naturally, take the choices the game offers, and let the count build; do not try to game it in one sitting. Which choices the counter recognises is not yet checked in the game. Because choices are per playthrough, treat it as missable in the sense that a finished playthrough's choices cannot be remade. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 500; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Fail at something, then succeed on the second try — the description implies a retry, so this trophy is earned by playing and failing naturally, not by planning. It will come on its own during a normal playthrough: any task you fail once and pass the second time qualifies, as far as the description says. Which tasks count is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the description reads like a random event or easter egg somewhere in Leonida. There is no objective to chase, so explore, poke at odd things, and let it find you. Where it happens is not yet checked in the game, and this guide will not invent a location for it. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the admission that the place is unknown is our own, from the official description.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a drive-by, but with a melee weapon instead of a gun. Slow the car beside a target, swing, and connect while still moving. Pick a quiet target rather than a crowd, and expect a few tries before the hit registers. Exactly how the game judges a melee drive-by is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the list; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts; PSN tracks the total to $250,000. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, so this trophy grows as you work the money trophies — rob, launder, repeat, and use your contacts rather than holding dirty cash. Which contacts launder bills is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of $250,000; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops; PSN tracks the total to $100,000. This one takes care of itself if you buy gear, cars and upgrades as you play — spend steadily rather than hoarding cash for the end. Shops of every kind count toward the total, as far as the description says. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of $100,000; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties; PSN tracks the count to 8. Garages cost money, so save for them as you go and buy each one when you can afford it — they also give you somewhere to store the vehicles you discover. Where the 8 garages are is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 8; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app; PSN tracks the count to 10. Find vehicles, then register them in the app — it pairs with discovering 100 vehicles, so register the interesting ones as you find them rather than leaving all ten to the end. How registration works in the app is not yet checked in the game. Sources: the official list on Exophase for the name, description and grade, and PSNProfiles for the PSN target of 10; the rest is our own advice from the official description.
trophies.name: On the Spot
